The Council has deliberated upon this matter. The corruption lies within `astropy/modeling/separable.py`, in the `_cstack` function that handles the `&` operator for compound models.

When `separability_matrix` encounters a nested `CompoundModel`, it fails to recursively evaluate the separability of the inner compound model. Instead of recognizing that `cm = m.Linear1D(10) & m.Linear1D(5)` already has a diagonal separability matrix, the code treats the nested model as a single opaque block.

The flaw manifests in the `_separable` function around line 306. When processing compound models with the `&` operator, it calls `_cstack` which incorrectly computes the combined separability. The function uses `np.ones()` to fill the correlation matrix for nested models rather than properly querying their internal separability structure.
